column1: # prompts.tsv — labelled corpus for --eval-skills (skill-ROUTING eval).
# One row per line: prompt<TAB>expected<TAB>provenance<TAB>split
#   expected   = comma-separated skill dir names (a PERMITTED SET — several moments legitimately map to
#                2 skills), or `none` (no ripwire skill should fire).
#   provenance = router  — wording adapted from a skills/ripwire-router/SKILL.md moment row; the label is
#                          that row's mapped skill (ground truth = the router's own moment map).
#                desc    — wording taken from a trigger phrase the target skill's OWN description quotes;
#                          the label is that skill (ground truth = the skill's stated trigger).
#                judged  — hand-written paraphrase (author-judged wording, 2026-07-24); the LABEL still
#                          follows the router's moment map, only the words are new. These are the hard set:
#                          they share no vocabulary with the descriptions by construction.
#                neg     — hand-written prompt where NO ripwire skill should fire (author-judged).
#   split      = test | dev — FROZEN HELD-OUT SPLIT (added 2026-07-25, round r26). The n=128 `test` rows
#                (43 of them `judged` — the hard, vocabulary-free paraphrase set that first made
#                bm25-desc's win/loss margin measurable, 24/43) are the committed benchmark and are FROZEN:
#                do NOT edit a description and re-measure against these SAME rows next round — that is
#                train-on-test with extra steps. Rows meant for iterating on a description change belong in
#                a NEW row with split=dev instead. 2026-08-08 (audit H1 follow-up): the dev split gained its
#                first n=20 rows (16 positive + 4 negative), covering the 2026-08-05..08 routing moments
#                (nest-profile/essential-complexity trust, cache-lint pack, --skipped-vs---doctor,
#                opt-remarks triage + its hard negatives) — free to grow or be replaced round to round,
#                unlike the rows above this comment. --eval-skills enforces this split (parses the column,
#                refuses an unrecognized value, reports test/dev metrics SEPARATELY with their sizes) —
#                this paragraph is documentation of that behavior, not the enforcement itself. A row with no
#                4th column defaults to split=test (back-compat for hand-built ad-hoc TSVs in other gates),
#                but every row actually in this file states it explicitly so the freeze is visible on read,
#                not inferred.
# ripwire-router itself is never a legal label: it is the fallback map, not a routing destination.
# Keep this file ASCII; the harness truncates prompts at a byte boundary when reporting misses.
# RELABEL log (2026-08-11, consensus content-gaps round): three rows relabeled on the S1
# ceiling check's two-rater consensus (blind protocol, sealed key; both raters independently
# contradicted the stored label — the only 3 such rows of 63 audited misses; record: EVALS.md
# "consensus content gaps" registration). Labels changed; prompts, provenance, split untouched;
# no rows added. Pre-relabel corpus lines (the sealed answer_key numbering — this comment block
# shifts later lines by +14):
#   line 180 (ceiling id M043) ripwire-orient       -> ripwire-mcp       (setup-health / "is my
#            ripwire setup broken" is the mcp skill's staleness/health surface, per the owner's
#            2026-08-11 tool-diagnostics fold-in decision)
#   line 225 (ceiling id M062) ripwire-change-check -> ripwire-find-bug  (a named failing CI test
#            with no known cause is a symptom-first localization moment, not a diff review)
#   line 233 (ceiling id M040) ripwire-fresh-eyes   -> ripwire-find-bug  (feature invisible at
#            runtime is a wrong-output symptom hunt, not a maintenance-risk pass)
# ── positives: judged paraphrases (author-written wording; labels follow the router map) ────────────
# ── positives: judged paraphrases, growth pass 2026-07-25 (S5.7.2 follow-up) ─────────────────────────
# n=16 judged rows resolves +-6pp; grown past 40 so before/after description-rewrite comparisons stop
# hiding real movement in noise. Same discipline as the rows above: each label follows the ROUTER's own
# moment-map row (skills/ripwire-router/SKILL.md), the wording is new, and NOTHING here was checked
# against what the current skill descriptions happen to match (train-on-test would defeat the point).
# ── negatives: no ripwire skill should fire (author-judged) ─────────────────────────────────────────
# ── negatives: growth pass 2026-07-25, kept proportional to the judged growth above. General
# off-topic prompts plus hard negatives that reuse a skill-name WORD in an unrelated everyday sense
# (orient/navigate/layers/merge/review/quality/efficient/graph/security/reuse/build/perf/test/fresh) -
# the same discipline as the original 4 hard negatives (talk-abstract review, commit/rebase wording).
# ── split=dev: tuning rows for the 2026-08-05..08-08 moments (nest-profile/essential-complexity/cache-lint/
# --skipped/opt-remarks). Per the header discipline above: NOT scored against the frozen split=test floor,
# reported separately, safe to iterate on next round without touching a single row above this line.
